newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Exchange official sees national bourse role.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Exchange official sees national bourse role.

text.p: Otto Naegeli, member of the executive board of the Swiss Exchange, said national bourses would remain the main marketplace for trading in the shares and share options of locally-based companies due to the greater liquidity such exchanges can offer.

Naegeli, who heads the Swiss Exchange's division on markets, told the Zurich Business Club on Thursday that his personal view was that local knowledge, historical ties, culture and language would keep national bourses as the natural marketplace for their respective companies.
Efficient electronic exchanges would also tend to pull back business from exchanges such as London's SEAQ International system as long as taxation and transaction costs were competitive, he added.
Naegeli said the Swiss Exchange had already noticed a trend for companies to return to their natural home-exchanges following last year's introduction of full electronic trading in Switzerland.
Naegeli also expected the emergence of "networked bourses," where local exchanges provide an access point to an international network of participating exchanges.
Stockbrokers or investors would be able to deal on all participating exchanges from a single terminal and exchanges would avoid the cost of setting up multiple trading offices.

The planned introduction of a single European currency was likely to lead to a concentration of trading in currency and bond futures on a small number of exchanges, each of which would be dominant in its range of instruments, Naegeli added.
